verbatim_locators.note: COVERAGE: whole article read; it has no figures or tables. A narrative report: no methods, results or limitations sections of its own. The reference list (102) was screened for integrity and the identities of references 38, 73 and 102 were read from the persisted JATS; the cited primaries were not read, so every number here is a restatement.

entries.proposition: DESIGN: the article is the report of a 2025 Special Interest Group; each section summarises the writing laboratory own work.
entries.snippet: The goal of the 2025 AES SUDEP Special Interest Group was to examine how seizures and their underlying epilepsy etiology

entries.proposition: EPINEPHRINE AS A PROVOCATION IN A DEE MODEL: in Scn8a DEE13 mice resting ECG is normal but arrhythmias can be induced with epinephrine and caffeine to mimic an ictal sympathetic surge; this is a challenge test in a sodium-channel gain-of-function model, not a treatment, and the sentence has no citation of its own (the preceding sentence cites ref 55).
entries.snippet: ECGs in these mice are normal at rest, but arrhythmias can be induced with epinephrine and caffeine to mimic an ictal sympathetic surge.
entries.anchor: Cardiac Arrhythmias Due to Ion Channel Variants, paragraph 1

entries.proposition: HPA CLAIM: chronically epileptic mice with HPA axis dysfunction have more SUDEP, and chemogenetic or pharmacological suppression of HPA signalling prevented it; the cited source (ref 73) is a 2021 review of HPA targets in epilepsy, so the primary experiment is not identified in the article.
entries.snippet: chemogenetic or pharmacological suppression of HPA signaling prevented the vulnerability to SUDEP
entries.anchor: Stress, Seizures, HPA Axis Dysfunction, and Psychiatric Comorbidities in SUDEP Risk, paragraph 1

entries.proposition: The reflex-hyperactivity mechanism is called established for the first time on the strength of ref 102, which is a 2025 preprint (bioRxiv identifier in the reference list).
entries.snippet: This establishes for the first time a potential trigger for SUDEP and identifies HPA axis dysfunction as a novel pathophysiological mechanism contributing to SUDEP risk.
entries.anchor: Potential Mechanisms Mediating HPA Axis Dysfunction and SUDEP Risk, last sentence

entries.proposition: A data set is labelled unpublished: the rabbit simultaneous EEG, ECG and capnography recordings behind the neuro-cardiac-respiratory sequence.
entries.snippet: leading up to sudden death (unpublished data)
entries.anchor: SUDEP in a Rabbit Model of LQT2, paragraph 2

entries.proposition: CITATION MISMATCH: the statement that SCN1B may not be a monogenic cause of Brugada syndrome carries ref 38, which in the reference list is a 1994 paper on EAG-related potassium channel genes in Drosophila and mammals.
entries.snippet: However, other work suggests that SCN1B may not be a monogenic cause of BrS38.
entries.anchor: Cardiac Arrhythmias Due to Ion Channel Variants, paragraph 2

entries.proposition: The human terminal-event series is nine monitored deaths (MORTEMUS), each a convulsive seizure with terminal apnea minutes before asystole; the authors call the data set limited.
entries.snippet: In the MORTEMUS study, 9 patients who died in epilepsy monitoring units with sufficient cardiorespiratory monitoring were analyzed.
entries.anchor: Seizure-Induced Apnea as a Mechanism of SUDEP, paragraph 1

entries.proposition: Stress axis: people with epilepsy are said to have elevated basal cortisol, increased further after a seizure; cortisol, not catecholamines, is the measured hormone in this section.
entries.snippet: PWE exhibit elevated basal cortisol levels compared to healthy controls
entries.anchor: Stress, Seizures, the Hypothalamic–Pituitary–Adrenal Axis, and Psychiatric Comorbidities in Epilepsy, paragraph 1

entries.proposition: Dravet syndrome carries the highest SUDEP risk (up to 20 percent) with a mean age at SUDEP of 4.6 years, a DEE-class figure from cited sources.
entries.snippet: While all PWE are at risk for SUDEP, DS patients have the highest risk: up to 20%.
entries.anchor: Channelopathies With a High Incidence of SUDEP, paragraph 1

entries.proposition: The report concludes SUDEP is multifactorial and that continued integration of human, genetic and mechanistic studies is needed; it ranks no mechanism above another.
entries.snippet: these multidisciplinary findings support the hypothesis that SUDEP results from the intersection of respiratory suppression, cardiac vulnerability, autonomic dysregulation, and stress-responsive physiology
